title: Non-Specific Address Queries
description: Rules for evaluating results when the user queries an address without a house number, or an ambiguous address that could match multiple locations (e.g., 'Main Street', '5th Avenue', 'Oak Road').

decision_logic.condition: Query is a street name only (no number). Result is the most prominent/central segment of that street in the viewport.
decision_logic.notes: Best possible interpretation of a non-specific address

decision_logic.condition: Query is ambiguous (e.g., 'Main Street' exists in multiple cities). Result is the most likely/prominent interpretation.
decision_logic.notes: Most prominent interpretation shown — correct disambiguation

decision_logic.condition: Result is a valid but less prominent interpretation of the non-specific address
decision_logic.notes: Valid match but not the most obvious interpretation

decision_logic.condition: Result is a business or POI ON the queried street (not the street itself)
decision_logic.notes: Shows something on the street rather than the street itself — marginally useful

decision_logic.condition: Result has no connection to the queried street name
decision_logic.notes: Not related to the queried address

exceptions: If the street is so common that disambiguation is impossible, Excellent is appropriate for any reasonable match
If the user appears to be searching for a business with a street-name address (context clues), treat as Business query

conditions: Result is the main/central segment of Main Street in the viewport
calibration_examples.reasoning: Shows the most prominent segment of the queried street — step 1 applies

conditions: NYC's 5th Ave is the most prominent worldwide
calibration_examples.reasoning: Most prominent disambiguation of the street name — step 2 applies

conditions: Result is a business on that street, not the street itself
calibration_examples.reasoning: Shows a POI on the queried street rather than the street — step 4 applies
